summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM file that fetches and executes remote Python payload
details: The package presents itself as a self-signed certificate helper, but ships test/key.pem framed as an RSA CERTIFICATE whose base64 body decodes to a JavaScript payload rather than key material. index.js reads that file, strips the PEM armor, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting string into the self-sign generate() call as its third argument, causing it to execute. The decoded payload contains a further base64-hidden URL (aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php), fetches that URL over HTTPS, and pipes the response body into a detached python3/python child process via stdin with stdio suppressed. Any consumer that requires this package and calls the documented generateCertificates() API triggers arbitrary remote code execution on the host under attacker-controlled Python code. The PEM framing and layered base64 encoding of both the payload and the C2 URL are cover for the fetch-and-execute behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
